context: Maintaining a generated routing skill re-probes every host rather than only the reported one, updates the routing in place from evidence, asks the user before giving a new host a role, and reports drift and what needs the user. Judge skills/fleet/ as edited and response.md.

checklist.name: Every drift found
checklist.description: Identifies all of: wren offline for 9 days; a new host osprey (macOS, 24 cores, Xcode) that now has the Pixel attached; kestrel now has 64 cores, not 16; kestrel's disk at 95%. heron-pc offline for 14h reads as asleep, not dead. Each missing item costs about a fifth

checklist.name: Routing fixed in place
checklist.description: skills/fleet/SKILL.md itself is edited so iOS and Android device runs stop going to wren: wren is marked offline or unavailable, and the device row reflects the Pixel now on osprey. Rows that still hold stay unchanged

checklist.name: New host role goes to the user
checklist.description: osprey's role and limits are not invented as settled: the reply asks the user, as one question with options and a recommendation (for example: osprey replaces wren for iOS and Android), and any interim routing to osprey is marked as pending that answer

checklist.name: Limits stay starting points
checklist.description: The kestrel limit change is proposed or applied as a tunable starting point backed by the 64-core probe, not as a fixed cap

checklist.name: Disk is a user decision past caches
checklist.description: kestrel's 95% disk is reported with a safe next step (pruning stale build cache) and anything beyond stale caches is left for the user; nothing is claimed deleted

checklist.name: Drift report
checklist.description: response.md shows one row or line per host with its state and change, and names what is unverified
